decision: Reject both co-resident norm/mix + attention layouts; production source, runtime and artifact root unchanged. Shared-program microbenchmark benefit does not transfer to the whole model.

design.description: Original two-worker norm/mix and fourteen-worker four-branch attention co-resident with independent five-BO runtime instruction streams and identical PDI/xclbin UUID. Three-branch layer-zero attention remains the existing program. Same device arithmetic/reduction order, state buffers and graph ABI.
design.grouped_all: Pair all eight R/K/V weight inputs and outputs, combine two first-rank inputs and four second-rank inputs. Static FIFO groups reduce stream count enough for both stages.
design.independent_second: Retain four separate second-rank weight streams to reduce multiplexing cost. Sixteen total shim inputs.
design.placement: Pin R/K/V cores across row two; first-rank cores columns 0/1 row three; second-rank cores columns 4..7 row three; norm/mix columns 6/7 row four. Explicit memory-tile group placement.
design.dma: Interleaved weights use innermost dimension 1024 and outer repeats <=64; R/K/V fill split into six tasks, first-rank into four, grouped second-rank into two. Existing packed weight BO contents unchanged.
design.invariants: 100 runs/token for fast BF16 decode, 960 logical nodes, existing persistent model buffers and transfers unchanged. No runtime or production compiler edits.

compilation_history: Pinned placement passed routing but initial interleaved transfers exceeded DMA dimension/repeat limits.
Chunked transfers compiled both variants; paired PDI bytes match exactly before copying xclbin.

validation.independent_second_full_regression: Not run: rejected after stage checks and whole-model performance screening.
validation.int8_full_regression: Not run: common attention path rejected on BF16 performance; production INT8 untouched.
validation.prefill_batch2: Not promoted or benchmarked; experiment changes only single-token norm/mix and four-branch attention artifacts.

benchmark.order: A1/B1/B2/A2, serial NPU; same release binary, different artifact roots. No compiler or profiler during timed runs.
benchmark.screen_scope: 48 samples; not a full ABBA acceptance experiment, and still slower than baseline.

profiles.scope: Separate instrumented runs: mean over four sequential input tokens [1,18,35,52] from zero state, including cold first token. Host execute/wait spans; not pure compute, configuration, firmware or DDR counters.

interpretation: Grouping layouts introduce throughput costs; widening the second-rank input helps slightly but does not restore baseline performance.

Attention span decreases by roughly 16-18 ms/token, while norm/mix span increases by roughly 26 ms/token. Isolated shared-program alternation removes overhead only when the program is already resident; the model still enters it after other programs.
These data do not prove that PDI byte size alone causes the regression, or that program switching cannot be optimized.
Independent co-resident worker graphs do not establish a hardware-bound model. Reusing cores and transfer routes across operation modes is the next program-sharing direction to test.
next_action: Prototype operation selection within shared compute workers and common DMA endpoints, first with a controlled norm/projection program, before attempting a persistent program for the dominant attention/channel/recurrent stages. Measure entry after a third program as well as already-resident execution.
host_validation: Release/test builds and 3/3 CTest passed before report commit.
